newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sells first raw sugar to Saudi.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sells first raw sugar to Saudi.

text.p: Australia's Queensland Sugar Corp said on Wednesday it would supply the first raw sugar ever imported by Saudi Arabia in a new 55,000 tonne deal.

Queensland Sugar Corp (QSC) chief executive David Rutledge said in a statement the raw sugar would be shipped in two cargoes to the new United Sugar Co's refinery in Jeddah, which was scheduled to begin production in early 1997.
Rutledge said the new refinery, which had a planned annual capacity of 500,000 tonnes, represented an exciting market opportunity for the Queensland sugar industry.
"We are confident that Queensland could become a major supplier to Saudi Arabia as the industry is well-placed to supply large shipments of quality raw sugar at a competitive price," he said.
Rutledge said the sale resulted from a strong relationship built up over the past four years wuith United Sugar Co, owned 15 percent by Britain's Tate & Lyle Plc.
The first shipment was due to leave Bundaberg on November 21.
Until now Saudi Arabia has imported white sugar to meet domestic requirements.
The opening of its first refinery had created a new market for raw sugar, Rutledge said.

Sugar consumption in Saudi Arabia has been steadily increasing over the past few years and was currently more than 500,000 tonnes, of which about half is for direct consumption and the other half for industrial use. Per capita consumption is about 31 kg a year, Queensland Sugar Corp said.
